text.p: These are the leading stories in the Algerian press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- "Terrorists" killed 47 civilians in two attacks in Blida region, south of Algiers. The biggest group, including a family of 15 members, was killed in Yemma M'ghitha village overnight on Sunday-Monday. Nine more civilians were slaughtered in Ben Achour hamlet the same night. Ben Achour is also located in Blida province.

- "Terrorists" slaughtered 26 people in Blida. About 20 gunmen cut the throats of eight villagers in Ben Achour overnight on Monday-Tuesday. Another band almost simultaneously attacked another village in the same area slashing the throats of 18 people, including 11 women.

- Gunmen cut the throats of nine civilians in Dira village in Sour el Ghozlane region, south of Algiers, overnight on Saturday-Sunday. The dead were all men aged between 20 and 40 years. The assailants fled in a car belonging to one of the vicitims.
- President Liamine Zeroual is expected to set a date for the local elections soon.
- Moslem scholars from Egypt, Saudi Arabia and Syria blame the Islamic Salvation Front for the killings in Algeria. Sadly the scholars are late in their condemnations.
- The Movement of a Peaceful Society's leader Mahfoud Nahnah faces growing demands by conservatives in his party wanting to sharpen the movement's Islamist opposition line.
